subject: Private deployment: onboarding checklist and network acceptance
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@medsight.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: onboarding checklist and network acceptance

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for choosing Redwood for your private deployment. To keep Day 0 smooth, I attached a short ops checklist and we put together a minimal set of network items we need confirmed before we schedule the activation window. Can you fill the sections in the attached ops-onboard-template.xlsx and return with the network topology (subnets, NAT/IGW, firewall rules) and an egress policy? Major asks below: 

- Public egress requirements (IPs / FQDNs) and whether a proxy is required
- Internal CIDR(s) for the LLM serving cluster and bastion access pattern
- KMS/HSM ownership and root contact for key handoff
- Any PCI/PHI constraints that require additional hardening

If you prefer, we can do a 30-min call this week and we’ll walk through the checklist live. Tentative internal owners: Ben (networking/activation), Karthik (runtime connectivity), Kimberly (security acceptance).

Attachments: ops-onboard-template.xlsx (spreadsheet with preflight questions)

Thanks —
Chloe Martin
Account Enablement | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@medsight.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medsight.com
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment: onboarding checklist and network acceptance

Chloe —

Appreciate the checklist. I filled the spreadsheet and attached our network diagram (medsight-network-map.pdf). Quick notes from our side: 

- Egress: we route outbound through a corporate proxy at 198.51.100.10; we can add NAT exceptions if Redwood needs direct IPs.
- Internal CIDRs: 10.10.0.0/22 for serving nodes, 10.10.8.0/28 for bastion/jump boxes.
- Keys: we use HashiCorp Vault (team: infra-security). They will coordinate with your KMS folks — security@medsight.com is on copy.
- Data classification: PHI in scope for inference inputs; full logging retention 180 days. Will need SOC2 evidence and an encryption-at-rest confirmation.

Two quick questions: 1) Does Redwood require a dedicated peering or is IPsec tunnel acceptable for initial pilot? 2) Do you have a recommended firewall port allowlist for model serving (we plan to restrict to TLS on 443 and SSH only from bastion).

Thanks —
Jordan
Director, Cloud Operations
Medsight Health
jordan.price@medsight.com
(617) 555-0189

[attachment: medsight-network-map.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: onboarding checklist and network acceptance

Chloe — forwarding Jordan's notes. High-level internal plan and blockers I see: 

- Egress/proxy: if Medsight insists on corporate proxy we need to confirm allowed hostnames (our runtime pulls model artifacts and possibly hits telemetry endpoints). Karthik: can your team enumerate outbound FQDNs and an alternate via proxy?
- Connectivity mode: For pilot, an IPsec tunnel is fine but we prefer a direct peering for production (better throughput and predictable latency). Karthik/Marissa: estimate work to stand up an IPsec tunnel vs. peering and schedule?
- PHI: Kimberly, please confirm acceptance criteria for PHI (retention windows, telemetry redaction).

I attached a short internal mini-checklist (redwood-privdeploy-mini-checklist.md) capturing the minimal gating items we want cleared prior to Day 0. If we clear these in 48 hours, schedule Day 0 for next Tue (8/10).

Ben Carter
Senior Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: onboarding checklist and network acceptance

Jordan —

Thanks for the fast turn. Confirming next steps and owners so we have a single thread for Day 0 acceptance: 

1) Outbound hostnames/FQDNs: Karthik will drop a canonical list and a proxy-friendly fallback (ETA: 24 hours).
2) Connectivity for pilot: we will stand up an IPsec tunnel for the pilot and run a 1-hour latency/throughput smoke test during Day 0. Marissa to coordinate tunnel config with your infra team (propose 8/10 09:00-11:00 PT).
3) PHI acceptance: Kimberly to provide redaction/telemetry controls we apply to logs and an encryption-at-rest confirmation artifact (ETA: 48 hours).
4) KMS handoff: Ben will reach out to infra-security at Medsight to coordinate Vault->Redwood key escrow steps and an ARN map.

If that plan looks good we’ll mark the checklist green and send a Day 0 calendar invite. Ben — can you kick off the HubSpot deal stage update and attach the mini-checklist? Jordan — if you can confirm the proposed Day 0 window (8/10 09:00-11:00 PT) we’ll lock it.

Chloe Martin
Account Enablement | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
